params.query: customer records unique real people identity dedup

params.sql:
select 'customers_master' t, count(*) n, count(distinct customer_master_id) ids, count(distinct lower(trim(email))) emails, count(distinct regexp_replace(phone, r'\D','')) phones, countif(rn=1) rn1 from `sahil-devx.dev_dna_silver.customers_master`
union all
select 'dim_customer', count(*), count(distinct customer_master_id), count(distinct lower(trim(email))), count(distinct regexp_replace(phone, r'\D','')), null from `sahil-devx.dev_dna_silver.dim_customer`

with d as (select lower(trim(email)) e from `sahil-devx.dev_dna_silver.customers_master` group by 1 having count(*)>1)
select c.* from `sahil-devx.dev_dna_silver.customers_master` c join d on lower(trim(c.email))=d.e order by lower(trim(c.email)), c.customer_master_id limit 12

with c as (select *, lower(trim(email)) e from `sahil-devx.dev_dna_silver.customers_master`),
dup as (select e, count(*) k, count(distinct lower(customer_name)) names, count(distinct phone) phones, count(distinct city) cities from c group by e having count(*)>1)
select (select countif(is_deleted) from c) deleted,
 (select count(distinct lower(trim(customer_name))) from c) distinct_names,
 (select count(*) from dup) dup_emails, (select sum(k) from dup) rows_in_dup_emails, (select max(k) from dup) max_per_email,
 (select countif(names=1) from dup) dup_same_name, (select countif(phones=1) from dup) dup_same_phone,
 (select count(*) from c where customer_master_id not in (select customer_master_id from `sahil-devx.dev_dna_silver.dim_customer`)) not_in_dim,
 (select count(distinct concat(lower(trim(customer_name)),'|',e)) from c) name_email_combos

params.query: duplicate customers same email different customer_master_id identity resolution

params.sql:
with c as (select *, lower(trim(customer_name)) n, regexp_replace(phone, r'\D','') p from `sahil-devx.dev_dna_silver.customers_master`)
select count(*) pairs,
 countif(a.city=b.city) same_city, countif(right(a.p,10)=right(b.p,10)) same_phone10, countif(lower(a.email)=lower(b.email)) same_email
from c a join c b on a.n=b.n and a.customer_master_id<b.customer_master_id

params.content:
## Customer identity / dedup findings (dev_dna_silver.customers_master vs dim_customer)

Question: "How many unique real people are behind our 1,600 customer records?"

- `customers_master`: 1,600 rows, 1,600 distinct customer_master_id, 1,600 distinct phones, 1,496 distinct emails (lower/trim), 1,575 distinct names. All rn = 1, none is_deleted.
- 103 emails are shared by 207 records (max 3 per email). In **none** of these groups do the records share a name or phone; cities/states/channels/signup dates also differ. These look like email collisions (probably synthetic/shared addresses), not the same person.
- 26 pairs of records share a name; none share phone or email (1 shares city). These are coincidental same names.
- `dim_customer` has 1,496 rows = one per distinct email. It is NOT a full mirror of customers_master: 104 customer_master_ids are missing from it. Joining facts to dim_customer by customer_master_id will drop customers.
- Best answer: ~1,600 distinct people (no record pair matches on more than one identity key). 1,496 is only a lower bound, from treating email as the only identity key.

Source: analysis turn on 2026-10-08.
